title: Renewal Triage - Parachute Plan and Escalation Ladder
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for high-risk renewals that need a fast, coordinated response (the 'Parachute Plan'). Use as the primary triage and escalation path for accounts flagged as high priority in the Renewal Registry. Focus: stop churn, preserve revenue, and capture learnings for product/eng and GTM.

Scope & When to use:
- Applies to any subscription renewals 90 days or less from contract end where account score >= 70 (see rubric).
- Also use if an executive escalation is requested by the account or internal AE/CS lead.
- Not intended for routine churn signals under 30 score — those go to normal CS playbooks.

Quick overview (headline):
1) Identify & score — CS Lead runs a rapid triage (24 hours).
2) Immediate containment — rapid-heavy-touch actions in first 7 days.
3) Escalate to Exec War Room if triggers hit (see ladder).
4) Implement medium/long mitigation plays (7–90 days).
5) Postmortem & playbook update regardless of outcome.

Signals & Scoring (triage rubric):
- Usage drop (30%+ monthly decline) — weight 25
- Support severity (open P1/P0 in last 30 days) — weight 20
- NPS/CSAT downturn (>1.5 pt drop) — weight 15
- Contract expansion/cross-sell at risk (pipeline lost or stalled) — weight 15
- Billing or legal disputes — weight 15
- Exec engagement decline (no C-level calls for 60+ days) — weight 10
- Score = sum(weights). Triage bands: 0–29 low, 30–59 medium, 60–100 high.

Immediate containment (0–7 days):
- Owner: Assigned CS Lead (primary), Solutions Engineer (SE) (secondary)
- Actions:
  - 24h: Kickoff call with customer (CS Lead + AE) to surface concerns and reset expectations.
  - 48h: Internal rapid sync (15–30m) with SE, Product PM, Support TL to align on mitigation options.
  - 72h: Deliver a short-term "bridge" plan: e.g., temporary increased support hours, priority SE time, or short-term credits (if warranted and approved).
  - Document all promises in a follow-up email and track as action items in the Renewal Registry.

Escalation Ladder (who to pull in and when):
- Tier 1 (CS Lead + AE): auto for score >= 60 or clear usage decline.
- Tier 2 (CS Manager, Support TL, SE Lead): add if unresolved after 72h or if there is a product/regression causing failure.
- Tier 3 (Head of CS / VP Sales): add if score >= 75 OR revenue >= $250k ARR at risk OR legal/billing dispute.
- Tier 4 (CRO / COO / Head of Product): add only for strategic accounts (> $1m ARR), multi-region regulatory issues, or when Tier 3 requests exec intervention.
- Exec War Room: optional 30m daily standups while active (owner rotates), with 3 bullet agenda: status, blockers, ask/decision needed.

Decision triggers for immediate Exec email:
- Collectively recommend offering a renewal concession >10% or multi-month credit.
- Product/regression cannot be fixed within 14 days and materially impacts SLAs.
- Legal/billing escalation that may delay renewal signature.

Mitigation playbook (tactical saves):
- Quick wins (0–14 days):
  - Priority triage runbook applied by Support: log, triage, escalate to on-call engineer.
  - Offer 30- to 60-day migration support (free SE hours) for onboarding friction.
  - Short-term credits or waiver of overage fees (coordinated with Finance).
- Medium plays (14–45 days):
  - Joint QBR with product roadmap alignment: showcase backlog items, approximate ETA, and mitigation.
  - Pilot a reduced scope renewal (lock in core modules, delay optional features) to preserve relationship.
  - Structured ROI/usage workshop with CS Ops to identify immediate value capture.
- Heavy-lift plays (45–90 days):
  - Dedicated eng taskforce to deliver a scoped bugfix or integration piece (MOU, SLA for delivery).
  - Commercial restructure: deferred payments, swap to annual longer term with volume discounts.
  - Offer migration to Dedicated/Private deployment if security/compliance issues drive risk.

Communication templates (use and adapt):
- Customer kickoff follow-up (subject): "Next steps after today's reset call"
  - Body (short): Thanks for the candid conversation. We are committing to: 1) immediate support prioritization, 2) a specific action owner (SE: NAME), 3) a delivery window (DATE). We'll review progress on DATE_2. Please reply to confirm.
- Internal exec escalation subject: "[ESCALATION] Account: <Acct> — Renewal Risk (Score: <score>)"
  - Body (short): TL;DR: <Acct> at risk — primary issues: <list 2–3>. Recommended immediate action: <concession/product/engineering ask>. Stakeholders requested: <names>. Decision deadline: <date/time>.

Approvals & commercial guardrails:
- CS can approve credits up to $5k or 5% of renewal value (whichever is smaller).
- Manager approval required for concessions between $5k–$25k or 5–15% of value.
- VP/CRO signoff required for >$25k or >15% concession.
- Any change to contract term or legal language must route via RevOps/Legal with Carbon Copy to Head of CS.

Operational checklist (to run live during a parachute):
- [ ] Triage score recorded in Renewal Registry
- [ ] Customer kickoff call within 24h
- [ ] Internal 48h sync scheduled
- [ ] Action owner assigned and SLA documented
- [ ] Commercial concession pre-approved (if needed)
- [ ] War Room cadence set (if escalated)
- [ ] Weekly executive summary sent to stakeholders

Measurement & success criteria:
- Immediate: reduction in support P1 volume and acknowledgement of action plan by customer within 7 days.
- Short: positive usage trend reversal (>=10% recovery) by 30 days.
- Medium: renewal signed or negotiated by 90 days OR customer converts to reduced-scope contract with clear timeline to full renewal.

Postmortem & knowledge capture:
- Owner must produce a 1-page postmortem within 14 days of resolution: what worked, what didn't, root causes, product asks, and suggested playbook updates.
- Tag the postmortem in Renewal Registry and link to Confluence page (template: CS-Renewal-Postmortem).

Playbook variants & templates (quick pointers):
- Small accounts (<$50k ARR): emphasize scaled play (automations, templated QBR), minimize heavy concessions.
- Midsize ($50k–$250k ARR): standard parachute with SE hours and possible credits.
- Strategic (>$250k ARR): activate cross-functional taskforce and potential C-suite outreach.

Open questions / TODOs (working doc):
- Decide whether Finance should have a standing delegation to approve credits up to $10k for mid-market accounts (current limit: $5k).
- Create a short templated MOU for engineering taskforce commitments to avoid scope creep.
- Instrument Renewal Registry to auto-alert Head of CS for any account entering score >= 75.

Appendix: sample internal war-room agenda (15m):
- 0:00–0:03 — Quick status update (CS Lead)
- 0:03–0:08 — Blockers and decisions needed (Product/SE/Legal inputs)
- 0:08–0:12 — Commercial ask and approval path (AE/RevOps)
- 0:12–0:15 — Action items + owners + next check-in

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a pragmatic, operational-first draft intended to be iterated. Please comment with concrete asks (approval thresholds, specific templates, or links to finance/legal delegations).
- If you pull this into a Confluence canonical page, retain the "triage score" rubric and escalation ladder as-is — those are core to consistent decision-making.

Document history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-07) initial draft
- v0.7 (2026-01-12) added scoring weights and commercial guardrails
- v0.9 (2026-02-18) updated approval thresholds and added war-room agenda
